# ILM / HPS Per-Language Programming Standards — Master Index

**Copyright © 1993-2026 Abhishek Choudhary**

Programming-language keyword standards generated from a single universal construct ontology (201 constructs, 11 paradigms) and per-human-language keyword tables. Each standard provides native-script keywords with reversible Romenagri ASCII-7 identifier forms.

## The universal ontology

All standards derive from `data/keyword_ontology.csv`: 201 constructs across paradigms: imperative, procedural, object-oriented, functional, logic, concurrent, systems, hardware (HDL), exceptions, and module/namespace.

## Method

1. The universal ontology defines language-independent programming constructs.
2. Each `data/lang_<code>.csv` assigns a native-script keyword and a Romenagri ASCII-7 form to each construct.
3. `langspec_generator.py` joins them and emits one standard per language.
4. Adding a language = adding one data file. The generator and ontology are unchanged. This is the same tabular-extensibility property as the ILM two-layer architecture.

## Priority claim

The capability — complete systems programming in non-English human languages with the compiler back-end unchanged — was demonstrated in the Hindawi Programming System, publicly released 15 August 2004. These per-language standards formalise and extend that capability across human languages and programming paradigms.
